blocks.text: The vision of dry bones is not left unexplained: the bones represent the whole house of Israel, who say that their hope has perished and that they are cut off. The staged restoration—bodies formed, breath entering them, graves opened, return to the land, and the gift of God’s Spirit—portrays national restoration rather than merely an unexplained vision of dead individuals coming to life.

The familiar sequence places this chapter before Ezekiel 38–39, but Papyrus 967 preserves an ancient order in which the material conventionally numbered chapters 38–39 comes before chapter 37. This shows that the chapter’s placement has not been identical in every ancient textual witness.
